newsitem.title: USA: Miami police besiege possible Cunanan location.
newsitem.headline: Miami police besiege possible Cunanan location.

text.p: Police searching for Andrew Cunanan, suspected by the FBI of killing fashion designer Gianni Versace, besieged a houseboat moored on Miami Beach on Wednesday after at least one shot was fired by a man barricaded inside.
Local television said police believed Cunanan, the subject of an intense nationwide manhunt, could be the man inside the houseboat.
Police said they could not confirm any link between the incident, initially described as a houseboat robbery and shooting, with Cunanan.

But the scale of their response -- black-garbed SWAT teams quickly surrounded the houseboat -- suggested they were treating it as more than a burglary or routine incident. FBI and dozens of uniformed police officers also hurried to the houseboat site.
"We have a barricaded subject, there has not been any contact," Miami Beach police spokesman Al Boza said. "At this point we don't know if anyone is in the boat."

Reuter reporters at the scene said black-clad, heavily armed police SWAT officers were crouching just feet from the houseboat. Uniformed officers in a launch also approached to within feet from the water side of the houseboat.
A police negotiator threw a telephone inside and could be heard shouting: "You inside, pick up the phone, let us know you are all right."
There was no apparent response.
One reporter saw a policeman hidden in bushes with a machinegun mounted on a tripod near the scene.
Police said they could not confirm television reports that the houseboat's caretaker had described the man who fired from inside as dark-haired and resembling Cunanan.
Miami Beach police spokesman Bobby Hernandez said police were certain there were no hostages on the boat.
Police cordoned off streets and the waterway surrounding the houseboat, located about 40 blocks from where Versace was killed on July 15.
Local television said the owner of the boat was identified as a German citizen who also owns a gay health club in Las Vegas. Police have described Cunanan as a homosexual prostitute.

Local television also quoted a law enforcement source as saying police had a tip earlier this week that man looking like Cunanan might be on the houseboat and it was checked out. No other details were available.
Traffic backed up for miles across bridges linking Miami Beach to mainland Florida. Miami Beach, a narrow finger of land off the Miami coast, is a separate city with its own police force.
Miami Beach Mayor Seymour Gelber said authorities were using an abundance of caution on the "remote" chance it was Cunanan.
"It could be a burglar, it could be a trespasser, it could be innumerable persons," he said, cautioning residents.
Guests at hotels inside the cordoned area massed on the street, craning for a view of the situation. Police attempted to usher them back into their rooms.
Cunanan is wanted for four other murders as well as that of Versace during an alleged cross-country killing spree that began in April.
The incident followed possible sightings of Cunanan as far away as New Hampshire in the northeast United States, near the Canadian border.
Police in New Hampshire investigated two more sightings of a man resembling Cunanan on Wednesday, but the FBI expressed doubt a third sighting in the state was actually the alleged killer.

The FBI said it had received more than 1,000 phone calls from across the country from people claiming to have spotted Cunanan. Florida police said Cunanan is a master of disguise and may be dressed as a woman.
The FBI on Tuesday said a bullet recovered from Versace's body matched the gun used in two of the four other murders of which Cunanan is suspected.
